title: Expecting a Baby? Five Tips To Help You Prepare for Pregnancy Costs
summary: The cost of having a baby is frustratingly difficult to predict. The actual amount families pay varies widely. Here are five tips to help you prepare for the often-unexpected costs of pregnancy and giving birth.

title: A Few Miles From the US Capitol, Dozens Slept in Their Cars, Waiting for Free Care
summary: If you’ve heard about how people are struggling with affording healthcare but haven’t been touched by it or seen it, then this pop-up clinic just outside Washington, D.C., put the problem on full display.

title: Georgia Helped Inspire the Medicaid Work Rules. Its Own Rules Could Soon End.
summary: For years, Georgia was the only state to require some Medicaid enrollees to work to obtain and keep coverage. Those rules could expire just as the federal Medicaid work requirements they helped inspire roll out across most of the country.

title: A GOP Congressman Backed Medicaid Work Requirements. His Voters Might Be Exempt.
summary: A California congressman voted for the GOP’s One Big Beautiful Bill, which is projected to reduce Medicaid spending by $900 billion. Now Rep. David Valadao, whose House race will help decide control of Congress, is telling his constituents they may not have to follow the new rules.

title: Medicare Drug Plans Are Hiking Premiums While Trump Claims Victory on Medicine Prices
summary: Millions of Medicare enrollees who buy stand-alone prescription drug plans will see their average monthly premiums rise by 50% in 2027, a new analysis finds. But enrollees can avoid the average increase by switching to lower-cost plans.

title: Your Phone Knows You’re at the Doctor, and Data Brokers Do, Too — Then Profit From It
summary: The Federal Trade Commission told a data company it could no longer sell data it collected from hundreds of millions of Americans’ mobile devices when people visited hospitals, dialysis clinics, or abortion clinics. But little is stopping other companies from doing so. In the absence of federal protections, some states are passing their own rules.

title: Frights, Fangs, and Healthcare Nightmares in Winning Halloween Haikus
summary: This year’s winning Halloween haikus take on measles, the high cost of dental care, and AI-powered insurance denials.

title: For Californians Drowning in Healthcare Costs, Governor’s Race Offers Few Answers
summary: In California, healthcare costs are rising faster than income and inflation, and 4 in 10 adults in the state say they’re paying down medical debt. With the governor’s race in full swing, it’s still not clear what the candidates would do to fix it.

title: Listen to the Latest ‘KFF Health News Minute’
summary: The "KFF Health News Minute" brings original healthcare and health policy reporting from our newsroom to the airwaves each week.

title: Data Center Health Worries Animate Midterm Campaigns
summary: Opposition to the rapid emergence of data centers in states such as Ohio and Arizona has ginned up activism and unified voters. A range of public health issues have played into the resistance.
